note: Pricing assumptions for the climate portfolio: grid financing windows, credit redesign in ledger terms, bill protection, and the disaster preparedness and response package (CLI-7/CLI-8). Amounts are 2025 dollars unless marked; ranges are low / mid / high. Basis tags: sourced (a cited figure), scaled (a cited figure moved), estimate (planning judgment). Nothing here is a canonical input.

ledger_credit_scaling.basis: ledger CLI-1A $0.90T plus CLI-5 transmission ITC and 45X about $0.22T, against the model's $1.49T for the same credit set in 2030-39 (index/climate-carbon-model.md)

grid_financing.system_savings_basis: sourced: DOE National Transmission Planning Study (2024), $1.60-1.80 of system cost saved per $1 of transmission, $270-490B through 2050

windows.label: Federal construction and grants: lines no regional builder will build, reconductoring on federal power-marketing systems, plan-selected interregional segments
windows.instrument: budget authority, mandatory, available until expended

windows.label: Direct loan authority: a TVA-model federal transmission corporation, TVA, BPA, WAPA, public power and co-ops, at Treasury rates for 30-40 years, repaid from transmission charges
windows.instrument: direct loans under the Federal Credit Reform Act (subsidy cost scored)
windows.basis: estimate: subsidy rates for regulated, cost-of-service-backed lending are low single digits; BPA's Treasury borrowing authority is $13.7B rising to $17.7B in FY2028 and TVA's statutory debt cap is $30B (unchanged since 1979)

windows.label: Capacity contract authority: DOE buys up to half of an anchor line's capacity for 10-20 years and resells it (Transmission Facilitation Program model, expanded)
windows.instrument: contract authority backed by the Judgment Fund; expected net cost scored at obligation
windows.basis: estimate; the Transmission Facilitation Program's $2.5B revolving authority was nearly depleted after two rounds (DOE, Oct 2024), and two developers have since terminated agreements

bill_protection.basis: estimate: offset the modeled wind/solar credit phase-out's bill increase for low- and moderate-income households (bottom two quintiles, about 40% of about 140 million households) through LIHEAP-style utility credits

baseline.item: Disaster assistance appropriations, all agencies, FY2015-24

baseline.value: $22.525B, $7.9B borrowing authority left; authorization to Sept 30, 2026 after 35 short-term extensions since FY2017

baseline.item: Wildfire appropriations, Forest Service and Interior, FY2025

baseline.value: Cancelled April 2025; ruled unlawful Dec 2025; FEMA said in March 2026 it would release remaining funds and open up to $1B of applications
Parametric block grant for Public Assistance, a single survivor payment, higher declaration thresholds, shift flood insurance toward states and private market; most needs Congress

disaster.unbudgeted_basis: estimate: recent all-agency disaster appropriations (about $45B a year nominal FY2015-24, about $52B in 2025 dollars, before the $110B 2025 act) against roughly $30-35B a year carried by the extrapolated baseline (the FY2026 DRF plus base disaster programs elsewhere). A current-law exposure, not an agenda cost; disclose beside the Judgment Fund line in D4 tests

components.label: Standing pre-disaster mitigation fund (BRIC successor): mandatory, formula floor for every state and tribe plus competitive large projects, with anti-impoundment terms
components.basis: estimate: roughly 3-6 times the pre-2025 BRIC scale (up to $1B a year); NIBS 2019 finds federal mitigation grants save about $6 per $1

components.label: Post-disaster mitigation top-up: Hazard Mitigation Grant Program from 15% to 20% of disaster grants (replaces the $1-per-$1 supplemental set-aside, which would be pro-cyclical and unbounded)
components.basis: estimate: 5 points on about $20-30B a year of disaster grants

components.label: NFIP means-tested premium assistance for low- and moderate-income primary residences (at or below 120% of area median income, capped at 400% of poverty, non-transferable), with take-up outreach
components.basis: estimate: about 1.1-1.5 million eligible current policies at $600-1,000 average discounts plus 0.3-0.8 million new low-income policies; FEMA's own legislative proposal sets the same eligibility test (FEMA NFIP proposal item 9); Risk Rating 2.0 cut new policies 11-39% (Dec 2025 study cited by senators)

components.label: NFIP debt resolution: cancel the $22.5B debt with a multi-year reauthorization (to 2035) and a reserve rule
components.basis: scaled: CBO scored the 2007 bill's $17.5B forgiveness at about $1.2B net over ten years because repayment was not expected; face value $22.5B

components.label: Wildfire risk reduction above the current baseline (Wildfire Crisis Strategy completion, community defensible space, prescribed-fire workforce)
components.basis: scaled: the Forest Service projected $50B over ten years in 2022 ($20B on its land, $30B elsewhere); federal increment over FY2025's $7.3B wildfire funding

components.label: Extreme heat: heat as an eligible hazard, cooling-center and tree-canopy grants, CDC Climate-Ready States and Cities to all 50 states (LIHEAP cooling is in CLI-5)
Universal Survivor Application and estimate-based Public Assistance: program effect of faster, more complete aid (administration is priced in CAP-7)

Climate Insurance and Recovery Affordability Program: premium help for low- and moderate-income owners and renters facing wind, wildfire and hail risk, available from FY2030 without waiting for a reinsurance backstop; states must adopt CLI-8 codes within three years to keep it
components.basis: estimate: about 8-12 million eligible households in high-risk counties at $200-400 average help

components.label: Voluntary buyout and relocation program: 10,000-25,000 properties a year, receiving-community investment, renter relocation aid
components.basis: estimate: about $250,000 average acquisition (local examples near $214,000) plus about 10% activity costs (Curran-Groome et al. 2022), 75% federal share; Iowa buyouts returned a benefit-cost ratio of 2.19

components.label: Federal residential catastrophe reinsurance facility (Treasury): reinsures insurers' residential wind, wildfire, hail and (opt-in) earthquake losses between a state-level 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 year industry loss, 10% retained by insurers, $150B annual cap; only in states with CLI-8 codes and disclosure; flood stays in NFIP
components.d4: permanent (expected net cost scored): risk-priced premiums at 1.3-1.5x modeled expected loss build a fund; Treasury borrowing authority up to the $150B cap pays claims the fund cannot; a TRIA-style recoupment surcharge on all residential property premiums (capped at 3% a year, up to 15 years, about $75B) repays it; any unrecouped draw is a disclosed contingent liability in every D4 test
components.basis: estimate. Layer pricing: modeled expected loss in a 1-in-100 to 1-in-250 layer is roughly 0.6-1.0% of limit a year, about $1-1.5B on $150B; premiums at 1.3-1.5x cover it in expectation, and the cost range is pricing error, ramp-up before the fund accrues and draws beyond the recoupment cap. Anchors (sourced): U.S. insured catastrophe losses about $100B in 2025, 12% above the 10-year average (Gallagher Re); the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund carries $17.0B of claims-paying capacity on a $1.29B premium (2025-26) and leans on post-event bonds; TRIA's federal share above a program trigger with mandatory recoupment is the scoring precedent; Sen. Schiff's INSURE Act (July 2025) proposes a Treasury program above a catastrophe threshold

components.label: FEMA staff restored (+5,000), cabinet-level independence, Universal Survivor Application build and regional rebuild
components.basis: sourced to sources/capacity-recovery-components.csv; not added again

components.label: Future-conditions national flood maps (FEMA) and NOAA precipitation and coastal data
components.basis: sourced to sources/capacity-recovery-components.csv; not added again

freed_d4b_basis: Governing decisions, Oct 26: resizing CAP-7S from $300B to about $105B leaves about $195B less borrowing inside the D4-B investment envelope

channel.basis: D7: REV-C1 receipts split 80% Climate Dividend and 20% transition share; the general fund books a 25% income and payroll tax offset (CX) on carbon fees. Added receipts from the higher price and process coverage follow the same rule unless Espen changes it.

payment_rule.status: proposed by Claude Code for Codex, Oct 26; pending Espen
payment_rule.why: O5 is the only option that leaves the package at or below zero for the general fund in FY2040 and FY2050 in all four cases, so the package's permanent pieces (disaster D2-D8, farm payments, bill protection) are paid at maturity by the fee that causes them. It costs households far less than O3: process receipts leave the dividend only in years the package would otherwise draw on the general fund. O2 barely moves the general fund. O3 raises more but takes about $90-170 a year from each quintile's dividend over 2030-39. Under O5 the combustion fee keeps D7's 80/20 split untouched. Corrected after review (Oct 26): an earlier O5 also spent the $150 step's transition share, which the shared ledger already credits to CLI-5; without it O5 still meets the maturity test but its 2030-39 result is about +$21B (central), not -$68B.
